title: Using AI as a Writing Assistant
description: How to use AI as a collaborative writing partner — from brainstorming and outlining to drafting and refining — while keeping your voice.

data.text: AI can transform how you write — not by writing for you, but by taking care of the parts that slow you down: staring at a blank page, restructuring a messy draft, or finding the right words for a tricky sentence. The key insight is that AI works best as a collaborator on the process, not a replacement for your judgment.
Where AI genuinely helps in writing

data.caption: AI can assist at every stage of the writing process — but your thinking and judgment guide each step

rows: "Create a 5-section outline for a [type] article on [topic]"
"Expand these bullet points into a paragraph: [bullets]"
"Write the introduction using this outline and tone: [spec]"
"Rewrite this more clearly, keeping all key points: [text]"
"Check for grammar, awkward phrasing, and redundancy"
"Suggest 5 ways to say [idea] in a [tone] tone"

data.text: The biggest risk with AI writing assistance is generic output. AI by default produces careful, inoffensive, middle-of-the-road prose. Your voice — your distinctive rhythm, humor, directness, or warmth — requires explicit instruction.

rows: Show a sample of your writing
"Match the style and voice of this sample: [paste 1-2 paragraphs you wrote]"
"Write in a direct, slightly irreverent tone — like a knowledgeable friend, not a textbook"
Specify what NOT to sound like
"Avoid corporate filler words like leverage, synergy, impactful. No bullet overload."
"When you made a stylistic choice, note it in [brackets] so I can revise it"
Treat AI output as a strong first draft — read every sentence out loud before using it

data.title: Generate angles (beats blank page)
data.content: "I am writing a [article / blog post / LinkedIn post] about [topic] for an audience of [description]. Give me 8 different angles or hooks I could take. For each, describe it in one sentence and say why it would resonate with that audience."

data.title: Expand notes into a draft section
data.content:
"Here are my raw notes for a section:
[paste notes]

Write a draft of this section (~250 words). Tone: [describe]. Match the writing style of this sample: [paste 2-3 sentences of your writing]. Do not add facts I have not included. Mark any gap you spotted in [brackets]."

data.title: Feedback pass on existing draft
data.content:
"I wrote this article draft. Give me specific, actionable feedback on: (1) clarity — which sentences are confusing? (2) structure — does the flow make sense? (3) length — what could be cut without losing value? (4) opening — does the first paragraph create enough reason to keep reading?

Draft: [paste]"

data.text: What AI cannot replace in writing

items: Original ideas and fresh perspectives — AI recombines existing patterns; novel insight still comes from you
Firsthand experience and anecdotes — AI cannot write authentically about what happened to you
Emotional truth — AI produces emotionally plausible text, not felt experience
Audience intuition — AI cannot know your specific reader the way you do
Fact verification — AI will confidently fill in details it does not know

data.title: The right mental model
data.text: Think of AI as scaffolding — something that holds the structure while you do the real work, then comes down when you are done. Use it to reduce friction, not to replace judgment.

data.title: AI writing assistant principles
points: AI is most valuable at the stages that create friction: blank page, restructuring, and rewriting
Show AI a sample of your writing to get output that matches your voice
Specify tone, what to avoid, and audience — explicitly
First drafts from AI are starting points; every sentence should pass through your judgment
AI cannot replace original ideas, firsthand experience, or audience intuition

data.text: AI writing quality improves when editing is separated into passes: structure, clarity, and voice. This prevents over-editing and helps preserve author intent while using AI for speed.
